body: Cloud providers charge using a pay-as-you-go pricing model, so you pay for the resources you use instead of buying hardware first. Traditional IT relies on capital expenditure (CapEx): money spent up front on physical items such as servers, network equipment and datacentre space. Cloud services are paid for as they are consumed over time, which makes them an operational expenditure (OpEx). Comparing the two shows why the cloud has no up-front hardware cost, and why you can add resources when demand rises and release them when it falls. Because you pay for what you consume, your costs follow your usage.
